forecasts.question: Will Iran publicly commit to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations (a named Iranian official or MFA announces readiness for talks) before EOD 2026-09-06?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO at horizon. Pezeshkian's September 1 SCO statement ('Iran will return to ceasefire if US does the same') is a conditional offer; per ambiguity_rule, conditional or preconditioned offers = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition. Trump stated August 27 'we don't want to speak to them'; no US acceptance followed. No unconditional named-official Iranian commitment to talks was published by EOD September 6.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-06, a named Iranian official (FM Araghchi, Supreme National Security Council, or IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV quoting an official) issues a public statement committing to resuming or entering mediated ceasefire negotiations with the United States. A 'readiness for talks' declaration counts; mere written-message relay does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official, OR Iranian state media (IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional or preconditioned offers ('will talk if US stops strikes') = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition; a mediator asserting Iran is 'open' without a named Iranian official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Araghchi or SNSC public statement committing to talks
Oman or Qatar mediator readout citing named Iranian acceptance

forecasts.question: Will a confirmed Iran-US indirect negotiating session (mediated, senior officials, named principals) occur before EOD 2026-09-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO at horizon. CENTCOM struck IRGC targets September 1; Iran retaliated September 1-2; CENTCOM struck three Iranian crude tankers September 5. No face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session was confirmed by any TIER1 source or mediator readout between September 3 and September 17. Iran's stated conditions (reparations, Hormuz governance regime, firm guarantees) and the US position ('not looking to meet') foreclosed the diplomatic track for this window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session (not mere message relay) between named US and Iranian senior officials/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar/Switzerland), between 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-17.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official mediator readout.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Message relay through intermediaries without a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump assertions of 'semi-negotiating' without Iranian or mediator confirmation of a held session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Oman/Qatar/Pakistan mediator readout of a convened session
Iran MFA confirms re-engagement or talks readiness
US-Iran bilateral halt in strikes for 72h+ (precondition)

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz reach >=30 vessels/day (7-day rolling average) before EOD 2026-10-03?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE. Ship-tracking data (GlobalSecurity.org citing RFE/RL, Straits.live) recorded 7 transits on September 9, 4 transits on September 15, and 12 on September 16 — against a pre-war baseline of 85/day. Of September 16's 12 vessels, 11 transited without AIS transponders active. The IRGC expanded its non-compliant blacklist toward 56 ships. September 1 US strikes on IRGC mine-laying assets and September 5 tanker strikes occurred without any IRGC commitment to halt operations. Insurance war-risk premiums remain prohibitive; P&I cover has not been reinstated by any named insurer. All three recovery preconditions (halt in IRGC activity, insurer re-entry, mediator-confirmed commitment) remain unobserved with 12 days to horizon. 0.22 → 0.10.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any AIS-based ship-tracking source (IMF PortWatch, Straits.live, MarineTraffic, Lloyd's List Intelligence) records >=30 commercial transits/day as a 7-day rolling average at any point between 2026-09-03 and 2026-10-03.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: AIS-based tracker + one TIER1 or OSINT confirmation (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval escort vessels and warships do not count toward commercial transit; if trackers diverge by >20%, flag AMBIGUOUS.

P&I war-risk cover reinstated by a named insurer for Hormuz passage

forecasts.question: Will Likud win the most Knesset seats (seat plurality) in the October 27, 2026 Israeli election?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE. Jerusalem Post polling aggregate across five surveys as of September 17 shows Eisenkot's Yashar at 22.2 projected seats versus Likud's 21.2 — a statistically near-coin-flip race. One i24NEWS poll (an outlier) gives Likud 27 seats and Yashar 22; Channel 13 gives Likud 19 and Yashar 22. Haaretz (September 17) reported the pro-Netanyahu bloc at 54 projected seats versus the opposition's 52, but this is bloc-level, not individual-party seat plurality. Neither bloc reaches the 61-seat governing threshold in any published poll. Yashar's marginal seat-plurality lead in aggregate polling warrants a small downward move. 0.42 → 0.40.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if official Knesset election results published by the Israeli Central Elections Committee show Likud winning more seats than any other single party in the October 27, 2026 election.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli Central Elections Committee official results, carried by Times of Israel/Haaretz/Reuters/AP.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Likud and one other party tie on seats: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (no plurality). Exit polls alone do not resolve; official preliminary results suffice if published before EOD Oct 27.

indicators.name: Polls showing Likud >=23 seats ahead of Yashar in survey average
indicators.expected_effect: +8pp toward YES (only one of five Sep-17 polls shows this)

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO before horizon. The Knesset completed its full four-year term and dissolved naturally on July 17, 2026 — the first time since 1988. Resolution criteria required either (a) Knesset roll-call confirming coalition loss of majority, or (b) Netanyahu announcing early dissolution with election date before Oct 27. Neither occurred: the coalition entered dissolution with a reported one-seat majority (61/120) intact, and the dissolution was statutory rather than early. All paths to YES are now definitionally closed prior to the Oct 27 horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

indicators.name: Smotrich formally departs coalition
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES (path now closed; Knesset dissolved)

indicators.name: Degel HaTorah files formal dissolution motion in Knesset
indicators.expected_effect: Knesset dissolved naturally Jul 17; this path is closed

forecasts.question: Will a named mediator (Oman, Qatar, or Pakistan) publish an official readout confirming active facilitation of a new US-Iran ceasefire or technical talks framework before EOD 2026-09-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 72h forecast. Pezeshkian's conditional opening at the SCO summit (September 1) and unspecified 'progress' reported by The Hill (mid-September 2026) provide marginal diplomatic signal. However, Trump stated August 27 'we don't want to speak to them'; no US reversal is on record as of September 21. Named mediator readouts confirming an active framework — not mere message relay — have not been published. Base rate of a confirmed mediator readout within 72h of continued US-Iran strikes: low. P=0.12.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-24, a named mediator government (Oman MFA, Qatar MFA, or Pakistan MFA/PM office) publishes an official statement or readout confirming it is actively facilitating US-Iran ceasefire or technical settlement talks, citing both parties. An unofficial or anonymous report does not resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Official government readout from named mediator published on their official website or carried by one TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera). Anonymous 'officials familiar with talks' does not suffice.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: A mediator confirming message-relay only (without naming both parties as active participants in a new framework) = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Social-media posts by unnamed diplomats = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Oman or Qatar MFA publishes readout citing US-Iran talks facilitation
Pakistan PM office confirms diplomatic shuttle between Washington and Tehran

forecasts.question: Will Iran launch at least one ballistic missile or armed drone strike targeting US military bases or naval assets in the Gulf/Middle East region before EOD 2026-10-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 14-day forecast. Iran launched ballistic missiles against US and allied bases in Jordan on September 1-2 in retaliation for CENTCOM strikes; Kuwait's air defenses engaged Iranian missiles on September 2. CENTCOM struck three Iranian crude tankers on September 5, drawing no publicly confirmed Iranian retaliation as of September 21. The established September 1-2 exchange pattern, ongoing attrition posture by both sides, and IRGC public characterizations of the ballistic response as 'proportionate' set a base rate of continued Iranian kinetic response. 14-day window from September 21. P=0.40.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, between 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-05, CENTCOM, DoD, or a named GCC state confirms an Iranian ballistic missile or armed drone strike targeting US military forces, bases, or naval vessels in the Gulf or broader Middle East region. A strike that Iran claims but US/GCC denies requires two independent TIER1 sources for YES resolution.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM official press release OR DoD statement OR two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Stars and Stripes) confirming the strike. IRGC claim alone does not suffice.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Drone or missile intercepted before reaching a US target but confirmed as having been launched against US forces counts as YES. Iranian attack on a non-US vessel or non-US base in the region = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless US forces were the declared target.

indicators.name: CENTCOM or DoD confirms incoming Iranian ballistic/drone attack against US targets
GCC state (Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar) activates air defense against Iranian projectiles
IRGC state media announces retaliatory operation against US military targets
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES (requires TIER1 corroboration for resolution)

forecasts.question: Will the United States and Iran agree to a formal halt in strikes (ceasefire or de-escalation framework confirmed by both named parties) lasting at least 14 consecutive days before EOD 2026-12-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 71-day forecast. The June 2026 MOU demonstrated that a formal halt is structurally achievable: the April 8 ceasefire held for approximately 30 days before fraying. Pezeshkian's September 1 conditional openness and The Hill's mid-September 'progress' report provide marginal diplomatic signal. However, the MOU collapsed July 8 and formally expired August 17; the US has stated no desire for talks as of August 27; and IRGC internal preferences appear to favor sustained Hormuz leverage over a negotiated exit. A 71-day window allows time for sustained mediator pressure and potential post-October-27 Israeli election dynamics. P=0.22 reflects the viable-but-unlikely pathway under current conditions.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-12-01, both a named senior US official and a named senior Iranian official (FM, SNSC, or President) publicly confirm entry into a ceasefire or de-escalation framework, AND a mediator or TIER1 source confirms that both sides halted strikes for ≥14 consecutive days within that framework.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Named US and Iranian officials confirmed in TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP) AND mediator readout or CENTCOM statement confirming the 14-day strike halt.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: An informal unilateral pause in strikes not confirmed by the other party = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A framework agreement without a confirmed 14-day consecutive halt = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A halt broken on day 13 and resumed = NO.
